::: {#sol-not-big-o}

We use proof by contradiction (@def-proof-by-contradiction).
Suppose $n \cdot 2^n = O(2^n)$, with witnesses (@def-witness) $c > 0$ and $N$.
Then $n \cdot 2^n \le c \cdot 2^n$ for every natural number $n \ge N$,
and dividing by $2^n > 0$ gives $n \le c$ for every natural number $n \ge N$.

Let $n = N + \floor{c} + 1$, where $\floor{c}$ is the floor (@def-floor) of $c$.
Then $n$ is a natural number with $n \ge N$, so $n \le c$.
But $\floor{c} + 1 > c$ by the definition of the floor, and $N \ge 1$, so $n > c$.
This is a contradiction, so $n \cdot 2^n = O(2^n)$ is false.

:::
